Over the past few decades, the
international order focused on promoting
peace and stability has been essential
to prosperity and social economic
progress in our societies.
Wars and geopolitical tensions that
characterize our times have had a
terrible human toll undermining
international order and consequently the
chance of prosperity.
That is why we must explore every
opportunity for dialogue, diplomacy, and
peace.
In the Middle East, the humanitarian
tragedy must end, and we must move
towards the two-state solution with
Israel and Palestine coexisting as two
sovereign states in peace and security.
The aggressive actions by Iran and and
its associated armed groups must cease,
including attacks on neighboring
countries, merchant vessels and civilian
infrastructures.
Similarly,
the blockade of the straight of moose
must end and freedom of navigation must
be guaranteed, including safe and tall
free passage, including through the Red

we must achieve a just and lasting peace
that puts an end to the brutal and
illegal aggression of Russia against
Ukraine.
Ukraine is a partner that has the full
support of Portugal and European Union.
In Sudan,
the most dramatic humanitarian crisis we
face must come to an end. We must also
remain resolute in combating the global
threats of terrorism and nuclear
weapons.
And in the face of the new challenge
posed by artificial intelligence, we
must find together the right balance
between innovation and regulation.
One that allows us to harness its
potential for the benefit of humanity
while preventing it from distorting our
very essence. Excellencies, the energy
crisis and the rising fuel prices we are
facing due to international conflicts
are affecting all our peoples. Everyone
is being armed.
From Asia to Europe,
from Africa to the Americas, no country
is immune.
They have serious economic and social
impact and are already having
undesirable consequences for all of us
and also for the parties involved.
This is a senseless crisis because it's
harmful to everyone. We must put an end
to this collective masochism and we must
do it quickly to close this chapter
which is a chapter that of widespread
widespread harm. We all have a duty to
learn from the lessons of the crisis of
the 1970s and avoid repeating what
happened then.
We will be judged by how
we handle this challenge. On the one
hand, it is urgent to put an end to the
protracted conflicts and on the other
hand, starting now, we must discuss and
decide on complimentary ways to mitigate
the impact of this energy crisis and
prevent its prevent it from being
prolonged. It is my belief that it would
also be beneficial
to discuss the mechanism by which
international oil prices are determined.
I do not have a concrete solution which
is very complex and difficult. But I
wonder if it makes sense for all of us
to be so dependent on speculation and
the volatility of financial and futures
markets which affect the entire
production sector
even when the instability originates
only from a portion or a limited period
of that production. excellencies.
We also bear the intergenerational
responsibility
to accelerate the energy transition
in order to reduce dependencies and
mitigate the effects of climate change.
I will share with you that in Portugal
we feel the devastating impacts of
climate change firsthand
in the increasing forest fires,
coastal erosion and the degradation of
marine ecosystems
and also
more frequently in extreme weather
events new such as storms, high winds
and flash floods.
That is why we take a strategic approach
to the energy transition. More than 70%
of our energy production comes from
renewable sources. We have anticipated
our carbon neutrality target to 2045. We
maintain close collaboration and
continued support for countries that are
particularly vulnerable to climate
change and we are investing in
innovative solutions such as agreements
to convert depth into green investment.
Climate change and freedom of navigation
share a common priority of our policy.
the sea and ocean.
Protecting the marine environment and
its biodiversity,
combating ocean warming,
addressing the threat of sea level rise,
and ensuring universal freedom of our
navigation are essential priorities on
the ocean agenda,
which is an agenda we all have to pay
attention to. These are shared
responsibilities and opportunities that
require a collective effort that must
unite us all.
Mr. President, excellencies,
despite everything,
despite everything, the United Nations
is a political masterpiece of humanity.
It will be constantly evolving and will
reflect
the decision of its members.
The results in maintaining peace and
security will to a large extent
depend on the decision by the members of
the security council and particularly
its permanent members.
For the UN to achieve the goals we have
set,
we must
we must make it more agile and
effective.
To that end, we must at the outset honor
our financial commitments. We must
provide the UN with the appropriate
resources so that peacekeeping missions
in which Portugal is proud to
participate
can make a difference on the ground
where they are deployed. We must strive
to make the security council more
representative which requires permanent
seats from Africa for Africa, Brazil and
India thereby reflecting
the changing world.
This greater representativeness of the
UN and its bodies must also extend to
language. Portuguese
is the most widely spoken language in
the southern hemisphere with nearly 300
million speakers worldwide. It therefore
deserves a more prominent role in the
United Nations. It is a language of
culture and business that across four
continents unites the members of the
community of Portuguese speaking
countries which celebrates this year its
30th anniversary and serves
as a forum for dialogue and cooperation
founded on a common history and a shared
language. Excellencies, starting in
January,
Portugal will bring to the Security
Council as a non-permanent member a
global perspective and the culture of
dialogue and bridge building.
We are deeply grateful for the trust
placed in us
by everyone and fully aware of the
responsibility that comes with it.
We are well aware of the challenges
faced by the least developed countries
and small island developing states. In
the security council, Portugal will be
committed to three big priorities.
Prevent, partner, and protect.
preventing crisis and conflicts with
severe human impact which are rampant
across several continents because there
are several and not only those that are

first or secondass conflicts. They are

cooperating and developing our
partnerships within a more transparent,
more representative and more democratic
council
and protecting protecting human dignity
by combating poverty and safeguarding
fundamental rights,
food security and the future of the new
generations.
Mr. President, excellencies and friends,
the magnitude of the challenges we face
demands collective responses. The most
effective response is a multilateral
response and the United Nations is at
the heart and should be and there should
continue to be at the heart of the
multilateral system. That is why
Portugal looks to the future with
renewed commitment to the mission of the
United Nations, with confidence in our
collective capacity and with hope that
it is together that we can build and
leave behind a better world and we are
going to do it and leave to future
generation a better world than the one
we are living in. Thank you very much.
